demonstrated_gap: Open gap 5 (independent-host recovery and power-loss durability unqualified) has no built-in native answer on the Claude side. The official sessions doc says session files stay on the machine that created them and plain resume works on that machine only. The first-party Python SDK adds an operator-owned SessionStore (0.1.64, with a 13-contract conformance harness and reference S3/Redis/Postgres adapters). Its session_store_flush='eager' option is documented for cross-process resume and crash durability (0.1.73), and it adds resume_drops_turn/resume_session_at guards (0.2.137), in-process @tool MCP servers and hook callbacks. It still runs the unmodified bundled Claude Code (0.2.160 bundles CLI 2.1.283). Anthropic's legal page lets an end user sign in to the unmodified binary with their own subscription, and the help center describes Agent SDK use on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan credentials, so the same-account check is feasible. The same trial also yields the first macos-arm64 evidence; both winners are untested there.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Use one frozen bounded research task with the same native claude login (no API key), model and effort on the WSL workstation and a Mac. Arm A (native): claude -p --output-format stream-json --session-id on WSL, SIGKILL mid-tool-call, copy the JSONL to the Mac and run claude --resume there. Arm B (SDK 0.2.160): the same task with a self-hosted reference Redis or Postgres SessionStore on the workstation (passing run_session_store_conformance), session_store_flush='eager', SIGKILL mid-turn, then resume from the store on the Mac with the same cwd. Adopt B only if it matches A on account identity and plan-usage attribution, exactly-once external effects, transcript completeness up to the kill and cache-read/token totals, and loses less state at the kill point. Keep native if copying the file recovers the same state, or if B needs an API key or any other non-native credential.

demonstrated_gap: Pi fills no gap for this requirement. It is a strong, very active MIT harness (formerly badlogic/pi-mono) with an agent core, a durable runtime and a TypeScript SDK. It reaches the existing accounts by re-implementing provider access, not by running the native clients. pi-ai lists its own OAuth logins for 'Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max subscription)' and 'OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription)', with credentials held in pi's CredentialStore. For Claude, this conflicts with Anthropic's rule that developers may not collect, store or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens. For ChatGPT, it bypasses the native Codex client's caching, compaction, tools and resume. Its ACP adapter pi-acp 0.0.34 advertises no session/resume or fork. The decisive reason is a requirement mismatch plus account-policy risk, not code quality.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Reopen only if the requirement admits API-key or multi-provider billing, or if pi gains a supported bridge that drives the unmodified claude and codex binaries. Then run the frozen task through pi RPC mode against claude -p and codex exec, and compare success, tokens and resume after SIGKILL.

demonstrated_gap: This layer has no gap for it today. It is the Claude counterpart to codex-acp, which is already conditional for ACP hosts such as DeerFlow. It runs the unmodified Claude Code through the Agent SDK over ACP, and was renamed from zed-industries/claude-code-acp. The ACP registry probe of 2026-09-25 shows claude-acp 0.81.2 advertising loadSession, session/list, session/fork and session/resume, the same set as codex-acp 1.13.1. It also adds an opt-in sessionFailure extension: durable, revisioned error and warning records with a category (connection/access/limit/...) and recommended recovery actions. It adds compaction and permission extensions as well, which gives structured recovery events that the plain stream-json path does not name. It releases often (v0.78.0 to v0.81.2 between 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-24). It matters only if an ACP host must drive both native clients through one protocol.
comparison_that_would_overturn: In one ACP host, run the frozen research prompt through claude-acp 0.81.x and codex-acp 1.13.x, and compare against native claude -p and codex exec. Kill the adapter mid-turn, then call session/resume. Score event completeness (tool calls, usage, sessionFailure category and actions), account identity (sign-in completed through Anthropic's own flow), exactly-once effects and tokens. Promote it only when an ACP-host requirement exists and claude-acp matches the native path on every check.
